fit: verified original ingredient or outcome scope
assessment: The aluminum chloride rat study compared isolated oral sesamol with vehicle and rivastigmine conditions and reported water-maze retention and biochemical measures. It introduces sesamol as a sesame-oil constituent. No toasted sesame oil was administered. The dementia-model outcomes do not give hours of Parkinson daily off time. Reference 19 concerns a mixed Ksheerabala preparation and is a separate family.

fit: verified original ingredient or outcome scope
assessment: Isolated curcumin reduced the cisplatin-associated prolongation of response latency at week five in a rat hot-plate assay. The change restored heat sensitivity toward controls. Other endpoints concerned nerve conduction and dorsal-root-ganglion morphology. The measured phenomenon was protection against thermal hypoalgesia. This is not a measure of clinical pain relief. There was no ground turmeric or Parkinson population.

fit: verified original ingredient or outcome scope
assessment: The Taiwanese Cinnamomum osmophloeum linalool chemotype supplied hydrodistilled leaf oil. Oral oil and isolated linalool conditions increased mouse open-arm time compared with corn-oil controls. Open-field movement did not differ significantly. The tested species, plant part, extraction and doses differ from ground culinary cinnamon. The mice were not a Parkinson population. Botanical presence and human customary oral exposure need independent characterization.

fit: verified original ingredient or outcome scope
assessment: Grape and wine are sources of monomeric and polymeric phenolics. The review draws on an animal anxiety-like behavior report involving grape powder and, separately, a hydroxytyrosol retinal-cell mechanism. The grape primary reference 259 was retracted in 2025 and supplies no eligible anxiety direction. The hydroxytyrosol source is a cell experiment, with no oral cold-pressed olive oil or anxiety result. The two source families are separate.
